title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). The experiment used a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine). A single shared initial candidate was generated per task by gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120). A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced intent constraints and workflow policies and triggered at most one repair when validator.violation_count>0. Outcomes: baseline success = 120/120 (1.00); guarded success = 120/120 (1.00). Contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We expand methodological detail, execution accounting, diagnostics, and reproducibility guidance grounded in archived artifacts to aid interpretation of this degenerate ceiling outcome and to recommend designs that reveal repair utility in future runs.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate natural-language intent into device-configuration commands, promising faster NetOps workflows. However, operational correctness requires more than plausible, syntactically correct text: commands must respect workflow constraints (e.g., shut-before-MTU-change), group invariants, and make-before-break policies. Prior work therefore proposes integrating verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers so that candidates are checked and, where necessary, repaired before enactment. Evaluating the marginal utility of such guardrails requires closed-loop executable tests able to detect semantic/network-level failures that text-only checks miss. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that isolates the effect of a validator/repair stage by presenting the same generated candidate to two conditions: (1) baseline (LLM-only suggestion) and (2) guarded (generate→validate→repair with an executable emulator). Our confirmatory question asked whether this guarded pipeline reduces emulator-observed semantic failures compared to baseline. The paired shared-generation design isolates validator/repair effects from generator variance; the run, execution accounting, and analyses are archived and referenced below.
sections.related_work: Benchmarks and tool papers increasingly emphasize closed-loop evaluation for LLM-driven NetOps. Executable testbeds such as NetConfArena and related emulation frameworks evaluate agentic behavior in an environment that can reveal semantic failures beyond syntax. Prior empirical reports and surveys describe generate→validate→repair architectures and guardrails (veto layers, canaries, model→formal-model translation) as promising mitigations. However, existing studies commonly conflate generation and validation effects by allowing independent generation per evaluated system, complicating attribution of safety gains. Our study complements that literature by holding generation fixed: we ask whether a validator/repair stage improves outcomes for identical generator outputs. This mechanistic focus clarifies one causal pathway reviewers and practitioners often need when debating whether to invest engineering effort in validator/repair subsystems versus improving generation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary design: The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1 and archived prior to execution. The confirmatory design is paired-binary with exactly N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks, deterministically assigned into three topology classes (edge, core, leaf–spine) with 40 tasks each. Each pair used a single shared initial candidate generated by the declared hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and presented identically to baseline and guarded conditions. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (reduction in emulator-observed semantic-failure probability). The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar at alpha=0.05; complementary reporting includes the paired-difference estimate and a bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration specified that repair_applied is permitted at most once per guarded episode and only when validator.violation_count>0.

Model, prompting, and generation semantics: All shared initial candidates were produced by gpt-5-mini under the archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json). Key declared model settings from the archive: requested_model = "gpt-5-mini", max_output_tokens = 1500, reasoning_effort = "minimal". The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 120 and stage accounting stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 120. The preregistered pairing parameter independent_condition_generation = false enforced that identical generator outputs were supplied to both conditions; this isolates validator/repair effects but removes generation variance from the confirmatory comparison.

Validator implementation and repair policy: The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) to execute intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks encoded in each task's payload (for example, must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break patterns). The validator outputs a structured validator_trace per episode containing validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and a boolean valid flag. The preregistered repair policy invoked at most one repair iteration per guarded episode and only when violation_count>0; repair prompts and repair_provider_trace artifacts would be archived if used. Because violation_count = 0 for all guarded episodes in this run, no repair_provider_trace artifacts were produced and repair_applied = false throughout.

Task bank and difficulty encoding: The task corpus is a deterministic synthetic set produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry contains: initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence of field changes (for example, shut→mtu→vlan→up), constraint metadata (allowed_fields, must_be_down_for_fields, protected_interfaces), and difficulty labels (level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}) plus numeric indicators (dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). These structured metadata permit stratified secondary analyses or reuse by future studies that relax the shared-generation constraint.

Instrumentation, contamination controls, and deterministic reset: The execution harness enforced deterministic emulator-state resets (container image checksum verification and deterministic seeding) between pairs to avoid state leakage. Provider-call audit logs captured hosted_model_call_event_count and cache statistics. Contamination heuristics checked for duplicate LLM outputs across unrelated tasks, cross-condition cache-key reuse, and emulator-reset checksum deviations; none triggered exclusions. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 120. The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) attests that all deterministic consistency checks passed.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes: The run completed the planned episodes (completed_episode_count = 240) and generated one shared initial candidate per pair (model_calls_used = 120). analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline successes = 120, failures = 0 and guarded successes = 120, failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both conditions). The paired contingency file (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records guarded vs baseline cells: n_11 = 120 (both succeed), n_10 = 0 (guarded succeed only), n_01 = 0 (baseline succeed only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents no technical or instrumentation exclusions (complete_pairs = 120, failed episodes = 0).

Confirmatory statistics and bootstrap degeneracy: With zero discordant pairs the exact two-sided McNemar p-value is 1.0 and the paired-difference estimate is 0.00. The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) returned [0.00, 0.00]. The CI degeneracy arises deterministically from resampling an empirical paired table with no discordant observations: every bootstrap resample reproduces identical paired outcomes (all pairs concordant successful), producing a zero-width empirical bootstrap distribution for the paired difference. The analysis log records bootstrap_resamples = 10000 and bootstrap_seed = 1729 in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Per-topology aggregated results: Tasks were deterministically assigned 40 per topology class. Per-topology archived outcomes are: Edge: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Core: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Leaf–spine: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40. These per-topology counts are reconstructible from execution/task_manifest.jsonl and scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/; representative scoring artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, which show normalized_response matching normalized_reference_answer and validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true.

Repair activity and secondary endpoints: The preregistered secondary endpoints (proportion of tasks requiring repair, mean repair calls per successful task) are vacuous for this run because validator.violation_count = 0 for every guarded episode and repair_applied = false across the archive. Consequently no repair_provider_trace artifacts are present. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty, and deterministic_reconciliation.json verifies provider_call_audit (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120).

Representative artifact diagnostics: Example scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json) include validation_before/after difficulty encodings (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count), parsed_command_count = required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and violation_count = 0. These structured traces demonstrate how the validator maps command sequences to semantic checks and produces operator-relevant evidence (which rules were checked and which fields were touched).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the ceiling outcome: The paired shared-generation design was chosen to answer a precise mechanistic question: does validation/repair improve outcomes when the generator output is fixed? Under that design the observed result is unambiguous: the archived generator configuration and prompt produced only validator-acceptable candidates for the curated task bank, yielding concordant successes for both conditions (n_11 = 120). Statistically, no discordant pairs existed, so the confirmatory McNemar test is uninformative for the preregistered effect-size target. Practically, this null/ceiling outcome demonstrates that a guarded validator cannot reduce semantic failures when the generator already outputs valid configurations on the chosen task set and prompt settings.

Methodological implications and recommendations: The run clarifies two complementary experimental strategies. To measure the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates, the shared-generation paired design is appropriate and yields a clean causal interpretation; however, it will return uninformative results when the generator is near-perfect on the task bank. To measure end-to-end operational utility of guarded pipelines under realistic generation variance, future confirmatory designs should allow independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true in the preregistration) or introduce controlled prompt perturbations and adversarial inputs to ensure discordant candidate quality. Additional practical recommendations supported by archived artifacts: (1) increase repair budget to multiple repair iterations and archive repair traces when used; (2) run multi-model comparisons under identical harnesses to assess cross-model generality; (3) expand synthetic task diversity or incorporate production-rooted incidents where data sharing permits.

Threats to validity: Internal validity — prompt and generator sensitivity are central: the archival model_configuration.json and provider traces document the exact generator and stage accounting, but results apply only under those frozen settings. Construct validity — the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 operationalizes semantic correctness via encoded workflow policies and task payload constraints; while reproducible, it simplifies vendor heterogeneity and partial observability typical of production. External validity — the synthetic deterministic task bank likely underrepresents noisy or adversarial production incidents; generalization to multi-vendor, large-scale deployments is therefore limited. Conclusion validity — the preregistered power assumptions (target absolute reduction = 0.15) presupposed baseline failure rates ≈0.40; the observed baseline success of 1.0 violates those assumptions and renders the confirmatory test powerless to detect the originally targeted effect.

Operational implications and auditability: Even when unused, a deterministic validator contributes to auditability: archived validator traces provide operator-facing evidence (which rules were validated, which fields were touched, and why repairs were or were not applied). The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts demonstrate how to instrument for accountable runs (provider_call_audit, stage_counts, and artifact hashes). Operations teams can therefore use similar deterministic validators to generate auditable decision traces even if the validator does not alter outcomes in a particular run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, producing n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The run documents a ceiling effect on the curated synthetic task bank and shows how a shared-generation paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects but can mask repair utility when the generator produces only valid candidates. We provide comprehensive archived artifacts (model configuration, task manifest, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts) to enable future studies that relax shared-generation constraints, test multiple models and prompt perturbations, and evaluate repair budgets and validator fidelity against more production-rooted corpora. Our principal contribution is methodological: we demonstrate an artifact-rich, preregistered paired approach that isolates validator/repair mechanisms and supply reproducible traces and execution accounting to inform next-stage confirmatory designs.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
